summary_en: The study compares music therapy with cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) to see which may reduce anxiety in people who have had cancer. Both treatments are given virtually through Zoom, as seven weekly 60-minute sessions. The record does not state a main outcome; the study is Phase 4.
summary_es: El estudio compara la terapia con música y la terapia cognitivo-conductual (TCC) para ver cuál puede reducir la ansiedad en personas que han tenido cáncer. Ambos tratamientos se dan de forma virtual por Zoom, en siete sesiones semanales de 60 minutos. El registro no indica un resultado principal; el estudio es de Fase 4.
who_for: Age 18 or older and English- or Spanish-speaking.
Prior cancer diagnosis of any type or stage, and free of cancer or with stable disease without progression.
Score of 8 or higher on the HADS anxiety subscale.
Anxiety symptoms lasting at least one month.
Access to Zoom and a quiet, private location.
not_for: Active cancer treatment completed less than one month before enrollment (maintenance hormonal or targeted therapy allowed).
Active suicidal thoughts, bipolar disorder, schizophrenia, or substance abuse.
Blessed cognitive score of 10 or higher.
Seven or more recent music therapy or CBT sessions for anxiety within six months.
Unable to give their own informed consent.
